{
  "subtype": "exploratory_data_analysis",
  "focus_variable": "visit_duration_min",
  "per_column": [
    {
      "name": "presentation_severity",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Clean ordinal scale from asymptomatic/preventive to life-threatening with well-separated, well-populated categories. A human can segment visits by severity and compare duration/urgency directly."
    },
    {
      "name": "symptom_type_primary",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Interpretable nominal grouping of clinical system (cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, etc.). Categories are meaningful and reasonably populated, enabling comparison of duration across symptom types and departments."
    },
    {
      "name": "intervention_urgency_level",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Distinct, interpretable intervention tiers (routine diagnostic to immediate invasive). Segmentable and directly relevant to duration and to the urgency axis of the query, though somewhat overlapping with the existing urgency column."
    },
    {
      "name": "medication_route_intensity",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Ordinal-ish escalation of treatment intensity (none to IV resuscitation) with well-separated categories; an external correlate of duration that a human can group on meaningfully."
    },
    {
      "name": "visit_context_type",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Clear encounter-type categories (acute new, follow-up, preventive, exacerbation, post-procedural) that are balanced and highly interpretable; strong segmentation variable for duration and reason relationships."
    },
    {
      "name": "acuity_signal",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": false,
      "rationale": "Dominated by 'not_present' (198 of ~250) with tiny sparse critical categories (4-19). Near-constant and too imbalanced for meaningful grouped comparison; also largely redundant with presentation_severity."
    }
  ],
  "n_predictors": 5,
  "relationship_informativeness": 0.7,
  "rationale": "Most added columns are genuine external, interpretable segmentation variables with well-separated, populated categories (severity, symptom type, intervention level, medication intensity, visit context) that let a human explorer group and compare against visit_duration_min alongside department and age group. They open informative relationships rather than restating the focus. Weaknesses: acuity_signal is near-constant and too sparse to compare, and there is notable conceptual overlap among the severity/urgency/acuity columns and with the existing urgency field, slightly reducing the distinct informativeness of the set."
}
